report_name: Falcon C2: Browser-Based Framework Targets Governments

threat_actors.name: Falcon Actor
threat_actors.description: The unidentified threat actor operating the Falcon C2 framework. This actor targets government entities in the Middle East and Southeast Asia for strategic intelligence collection and is assessed to be nation-state-aligned with a focus on operational security.
threat_actors.goals: Strategic intelligence collection from government targets.

attack_patterns.name: Drive-by Compromise
attack_patterns.description: Malicious JavaScript is placed on legitimate government websites, such as webmail portals, to infect visitors' browsers with the Falcon C2 framework.

attack_patterns.name: Command and Scripting Interpreter: JavaScript
attack_patterns.description: The core of the Falcon framework relies on executing malicious JavaScript within the victim's browser for command and control, data exfiltration, and payload delivery.

attack_patterns.name: Hide Artifacts: Web Session Cookie
attack_patterns.description: The Falcon implant uses browser localStorage, sessionStorage, and cookies to maintain a persistent session identifier.

attack_patterns.name: Deobfuscate/Decode Files or Information
attack_patterns.description: The Falcon JavaScript implant decodes itself at runtime from a XOR-encoded integer array to evade static analysis.

attack_patterns.name: Obfuscated Files or Information
attack_patterns.description: The Falcon JavaScript implant is dynamically generated and obfuscated using a single-byte XOR cipher for each victim session to evade signature-based detection.

attack_patterns.name: Application Layer Protocol: Web Protocols
attack_patterns.description: Falcon C2 communication is established over TLS-encrypted WebSockets, with a fallback to a Comet-based protocol over HTTP. The Antino implant uses Microsoft OneDrive, a web service, for C2.

attack_patterns.name: Encrypted Channel: Asymmetric Cryptography
attack_patterns.description: RSA is used to securely exchange the AES session key for encrypting C2 communications over WebSockets.

attack_patterns.name: Encrypted Channel: Symmetric Cryptography
attack_patterns.description: AES encryption, via the browser's native Web Crypto API, is used to encrypt all data exchanged over the WebSocket C2 channel.

attack_patterns.name: Software Extensions
attack_patterns.description: The Falcon framework is capable of sideloading malicious Chrome extensions to enhance its persistence and capabilities within the compromised browser.

attack_patterns.name: Masquerading: Match Legitimate Resource Name or Location
attack_patterns.description: The Falcon implant's session ID is stored using the key 'Baidu-Fid', mimicking a legitimate service from Baidu to evade suspicion.

malware.name: Falcon
malware.description: A sophisticated, browser-based command and control (C2) framework designed for strategic intelligence collection. It operates by injecting malicious JavaScript into legitimate web applications, primarily targeting government entities.

malware.name: Antino
malware.description: A secondary implant delivered by the Falcon C2 framework. It uses Microsoft OneDrive for its command and control communications.

malware.name: PeckBirdy
malware.description: A C2 framework previously reported by Trend Micro. The Falcon framework is considered a variant of PeckBirdy based on technical overlaps in URL structure, payload delivery, and communication protocols.

tools.name: Microsoft OneDrive
tools.description: Used by the Antino implant for command and control communications, helping the payload blend in with normal network traffic.

tools.name: Google Chrome
tools.description: The browser environment targeted and compromised by the Falcon C2 framework. The framework can sideload malicious Chrome extensions.

campaigns.name: Falcon C2 Espionage Campaign March-May 2026
campaigns.description: A series of campaigns observed between March and May 2026 using the Falcon C2 framework to target government ministries in the Middle East and Southeast Asia for strategic intelligence collection.
campaigns.objective: Strategic intelligence collection from government entities.

identities.name: Government Ministries in the Middle East
identities.description: A class of victims targeted by the Falcon C2 framework, including ministries of foreign affairs, defense, and interior in one Middle Eastern country.

identities.name: Government Ministries in Southeast Asia
identities.description: A class of victims targeted by the Falcon C2 framework, including ministries of foreign affairs, defense, and interior, and law enforcement agencies in four Southeast Asian countries.

infrastructure.name: Falcon C2 Server
infrastructure.description: The C2 server for the Falcon framework, which communicates with implants via WebSockets or a Comet-based protocol. The management panel is hidden and requires a specific keypress sequence to access.

infrastructure.name: Antino OneDrive C2
infrastructure.description: The Antino implant uses Microsoft OneDrive for its C2 communications, leveraging the legitimate cloud service to blend in with normal network traffic.

indicators.name: Falcon C2 Browser Artifact 'Baidu-Fid'
indicators.pattern:
title: Falcon C2 Browser Artifact 'Baidu-Fid'
id: f1a2b3c4-d5e6-4a7b-8c9d-e0f1a2b3c4d5
status: experimental
description: Detects the string 'Baidu-Fid' used as a key for session IDs in cookies by the Falcon C2 framework.
references:
  - https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/falcon-c2-browser-compromise/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-11-12
tags:
  - attack.t1564.006
  - attack.persistence
level: medium
logsource:
  category: proxy
detection:
  selection:
    c-cookie|contains: 'Baidu-Fid='
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects the string 'Baidu-Fid' used as a key for session IDs in cookies or browser local storage by the Falcon C2 framework.

indicators.name: Falcon C2 URL Path '/config/'
indicators.pattern:
title: Falcon C2 URL Path '/config/'
id: c4d5e6f7-a8b9-4d0e-9f1a-2b3c4d5e6f7a
status: experimental
description: Detects the use of the '/config/' URL path, which has been associated with the Falcon C2 framework.
references:
  - https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/falcon-c2-browser-compromise/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-11-12
tags:
  - attack.t1071.001
  - attack.command_and_control
level: medium
logsource:
  category: proxy
detection:
  selection:
    c-uri-stem|contains: '/config/'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects the use of the '/config/' URL path, which has been associated with the Falcon C2 framework and differentiates it from the related PeckBirdy framework.
